artboards.title: Today: the Main tab as built
Glance view (leading: bare, with the rail)
Option B: one paragraph at a time
Option C: tab bar stays, Read aloud button
Option A: bare, before the rail
New answer arrives: the full panel comes back

annotations.text:
Today, at true size (300 px wide).
Tab bar 20 px, chat row, transcript, then the dock: two chips of 30 px, the question box of 66 px, the Ask button of 36 px. The dock is 157 px, so the answer gets 412 px. Answer text is 12 px on a 1.4 line. Every value is from the stylesheet.

Glance view, leading candidate.
Only the answer, text 16 px on a 1.5 line. The rail on the right is the position: an arrow up, the stop you are on out of how many (1/4), one tall block per paragraph with the current one lit, an arrow down. The hidden spoiler counts as a stop. The rail takes 32 px of width, so the text gets 250 px.

The bottom line is allowed to wrap. Here it runs to two lines on purpose so the cost is visible: 14 px more, out of 676 px of reading space.

Option B: one paragraph fills the screen.
Text at 20 px. Down moves to the next paragraph; the rail shows stop 2 of 4. Best for reading across a room; worst for a checklist, because you cannot see two steps at once.

Option C: the tab bar stays, and the planned Read aloud button sits where the Ask button was.
LB and RB still change tabs, so a person is never lost. Costs 24 px at the top and 68 px at the bottom, which is 92 px of the reading space the other two options keep.

What each press does in glance.
Up and Down: move between paragraphs, the rail follows.
A on the hidden spoiler: opens it. A anywhere else: read aloud, once that exists.
B, X, Y, LB, RB, Steam: bring the full panel back. LB and RB land on the tab you asked for.
A tap on the answer does what A does. A tap on the bottom line does what B does.

Coming back is not a morph. The full panel appears with the same paragraph at the top and the ring still on it, and the bars fade in over about a sixth of a second so it does not snap. Measured on the Deck before it ships.

Option A as first drawn, before the rail.
Kept so the rail can be judged against nothing. Same text size, same bottom line, one line only.

The one thing to decide: a new answer arrives while you are in glance (from a spoken word, a chip read aloud, or a question asked from another device).

Left, recommended: glance stays. A thin NEW line at the top names the question that produced it, the new answer shows big, the rail resets to 1 of 3. You opened glance to read; the reading continues.

Right: the full panel comes back on its own with the new answer at the top of the chat. You see the question box and the chips again, and the text drops to the normal size. Safer if you meant to type next; jarring if you did not.

What is not from our code.
The dark ground behind the panel is Steam's own and is drawn here as #0e141b. The font is the one the existing mockups use, since the plugin inherits Steam's. Headings inside an answer have no rule in the stylesheet, so none are drawn. The questions, the answers and the chips are made up to show shape, not a real game's data.
